question: In a class of 100 students, the mean marks obtained in a certain subject is 25 and in another class of 50 students, the mean marks obtained in the same subject is 70. The mean marks obtained by the students of both the classes taken together is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assuming the base average as the lowest mean (25), the excess mean for Class 2 is 70 − 25 = 45.

Total excess marks contributed by 50 students of Class 2 = 45 × 50 = 2250.

Distributing this excess equally among all students (100 + 50) = 2250 ÷ 150 = 15.

Combined mean = Base average + Net distributed excess = 25 + 15 = 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Class 1: Students (n₁) = 100, Mean marks (x₁) = 25

Class 2: Students (n₂) = 50, Mean marks (x₂) = 70

**Formula Used:**

Combined Mean = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)
